input_references.role: Complete timestamped GPS table linked to the trip summary by trajectory_id

metadata.goal: Understand how taxi service departs from its dominant operating pattern and what forms those departures take.
metadata.dataset_description: 30 curated taxi trips with linked timestamped GPS points. Ordinary traces retain their source cadence. Four near-stationary traces are reconstructed at 1.7–3 second intervals on cached OSRM road positions; trip_21 has a constructed 24-second stationary observation window. These four traces are derived observations, not unmodified raw GPS records. Pickup channels for trip_07 (A: dispatch) and trip_20 (C: street request) are constructed to represent cross-channel exceptions. Original channel fields are retained in source_* columns; origin_call and origin_stand are synchronized with the constructed channels.

insight_list.insight: Most selected trips remain within the dominant Porto service network, while a small number extend much farther toward the metropolitan edges.

plot.title: Spatial Extent of Taxi Trips
plot.description: Grey lines show the compact service-network trips; red lines identify the four trajectories whose observed distance exceeds 20 km.

insight_list.question: Which trajectories extend beyond the spatial footprint of the dominant Porto taxi service network?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Use route extent to distinguish metropolitan-edge trips from the compact service-network pattern.

insight_list.insight: Very short or nearly stationary completed trips form a distinct exception to the longer moving trips and need to be interpreted separately from ordinary city crossings.

plot.title: Movement-Support Anomalies
plot.description: Trip duration and travelled distance identify near-stationary trips; the enlarged panel shows their sub-metre movement and GPS sample counts.

insight_list.question: Which completed trips are unusually short or nearly stationary, based on elapsed duration and distance travelled?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Separate extremely short-duration, near-stationary movement records from spatially extended trips before interpreting service anomalies.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
d=df.copy(); d['minimal_movement']=(d.duration_seconds<=30)&(d.distance_km<=.01)
plt.scatter(d.duration_seconds/60,d.distance_km,c=d.minimal_movement.map({True:'#f59e0b',False:'#94a3b8'})); plt.xlabel('duration (minutes)'); plt.ylabel('distance travelled (km)'); print(d[d.minimal_movement][['trajectory_id','duration_seconds','distance_km','point_count']])

insight_list.insight: The exceptional trips are not confined to one pickup channel: unusual spatial extent and unusual local movement both occur across different service contexts.

plot.title: Service-Channel Profile of Anomaly Types
plot.description: The heatmap cross-tabulates anomaly type and pickup channel for distinct trips, rather than reusing the spatial map.

insight_list.question: How do pickup channels differ between extended-range and minimal-movement exceptions?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare anomaly type with pickup channel to avoid treating all exceptional trips as one service-context phenomenon.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
d=df.copy(); d['anomaly_type']='regular'; d.loc[d.distance_km>=20,'anomaly_type']='extended-range'; d.loc[(d.duration_seconds<=30)&(d.distance_km<=.01),'anomaly_type']='minimal-movement'; print(pd.crosstab(d[d.anomaly_type!='regular'].anomaly_type,d[d.anomaly_type!='regular'].call_type))

summary: Most selected trips remain within the dominant Porto service network, while a small number extend to metropolitan edges. Very short or nearly stationary completed trips form a separate exception to longer moving trips. Together, the exception types occur across more than one pickup channel and therefore represent different service contexts.
